dataset.description: This project is a simple, georeferenced rockpool survey designed to generate FAIR example data for training. At ~10 coastal sites, we record basic water measurements (temperature, salinity, depth) and photograph visible organisms, then compile a structured spreadsheet of sampling metadata, measurements, and species occurrences standardized with authoritative vocabularies (e.g., WoRMS).

format:
This project will create field observational data from rocky-shore rockpools, combining tabular measurements, geospatial information, and photographic records of observed invertebrates. Specifically, we will generate:

Tabular field records / measurements: pool ID, date/time, GPS coordinates (lat/long), water temperature, salinity, maximum depth, and initial species names recorded in the field.

Formats: CSV (primary), and possibly XLSX during data entry (converted to CSV for sharing/archiving).

Geospatial data: sampling locations recorded as latitude/longitude (WGS84) within the spreadsheet; optionally exported as a simple geospatial file for mapping.

Formats: CSV (lat/long columns); optional GeoJSON.

Images of organisms and habitats: photos of visible invertebrates in each rockpool, linked to the pool ID and image number (e.g., pool01_image01.jpg).

Formats: JPG/JPEG

Derived/curated taxonomy identifiers: post-field enrichment of observed species names with persistent identifiers (e.g., WoRMS).

Formats: included as additional columns in the CSV.

Documentation and metadata: data dictionary describing columns/units, sampling protocol notes, and README describing folder structure and naming conventions for images.

Formats: TXT

dmp.description:
**** Example DMP ****

This TNA project is a short field-to-lab survey of rocky-shore rockpools aimed at documenting biodiversity patterns and basic water properties across multiple coastal locations. Samples/observations will be collected from ~10 rockpools along a defined shoreline transect, with each site assigned a unique Pool ID. For each pool, geographic coordinates (latitude/longitude) and contextual information (date/time, site notes) will be recorded, and simple environmental measurements will be taken using handheld sensors (e.g., water temperature in °C, salinity in PSU, maximum depth in m).

The project will generate two main datasets: (1) a structured spreadsheet containing sampling event metadata, georeferenced measurements, and species occurrence records linked to each Pool ID; and (2) a set of digital images (context photos and organism photos) captured per pool, named using a consistent convention and linked to the spreadsheet via Pool ID and image identifiers. Species names will be standardized using an authoritative taxonomy (e.g., WoRMS with AphiaIDs), and measurement variables will be recorded with clear units and controlled terms to support reuse, integration, and publication in relevant repositories.
